## Learning objectives (planned)

By the end of this chapter you will be able to:

- Distinguish the ways a project ends: completion, extinction, addition, integration, starvation.
- Run an orderly administrative closeout: deliverable acceptance, contract closure, financial closure.
- Release resources and transition the product to operations or the customer.
- Facilitate a lessons-learned review and write to the organizational knowledge base.
- Explain the organizational and human implications of closing a project (team dispersal, morale).
- Recognise when to terminate a troubled project early, and how to do it responsibly.

## Topic outline

1. Types of project termination.
2. The closeout checklist: scope verification, punch list, sign-off.
3. Contract and procurement closure.
4. Financial closure and final cost accounting.
5. Lessons learned and the post-implementation review.
6. Resource release and team transition.
7. Early termination: decision criteria and stakeholder communication.
8. Running case: closing out the RC-vehicle prototype project and handing off to manufacturing.
